author: Raikousen
content:
https://classic.wowhead.com/talent-calc/paladin/055030223--501053512200151 

This is what I play with on my 60 Paladin.  My main objective is to heal in battlegrounds, namely WSG, but also have access to Repentance as it's a useful pvp cc.  There's a few points of wiggle room in Retribution, and since you're full ret you obviously can kill monsters/deliver a SoC whack on a player if you don't need to heal.   Missing Divine Favor and Holy Power obviously is a disadvantage, but mana longevity isn't the final factor in PVP healing, especially vanilla where combat is fast and deadly.  Going deep holy/protection of course makes a more reliable healer, but I like being able to use Repentance and give the enemy a two handed holy strike sometimes.

author: maddmax89
content: Hey guys. I have a questiong about pala tanking. I'm lvl 22 right now and currently using this build https://talents.turtle-wow.org/paladin/0-5KPL0JU6-50UVCC, I didn't know the talent order, so I decided to take 5 points in redoubt, 3 points in precision, 1 point in guiardian favor, and 1 point in toughness. Then I took Blessing of Sanctuary and 2 points in Improved righteous fury. And even I was lvl 22, I cold not hold aggro properly sometimes. Mostly I think the problem is mana. Consecration lvl 1 takes 120 mana, its really expensive for the start imo, considering you have to use crusader strikes, and holy strike on mobs, and also renew seal of Righteousness to do some holy damage to mobs to hold aggro. I tried to buff myself with Blessing of Sanctuary, since it reduces incoming damage and strikes back with holy damage, but then mana problem becomes more sufficient. I've been told that BoS is a really good thing for prot palas and you should use it first thing. After I realised I have mana problems, I tried to use Blessing of Wisdom on myself, to have some mana regen. So question is what blessing should I use in low lvl dungeons to hold aggro and do not drink every pool, and also should I use Consecration often or not, since it's not cheap, and it makes me to drink very often, not doing to much damage? I always thought that pala tanking in Vanilla is easier then warrior, since you dont have to switch stances and you have consecration which does aoe damage and holds aggro. And since pala on Twow are improved compared to standart Vanilla/Classic palas, I thought it would be a piece of cake. And it wasn't the case when I tanked DM yesterday. Either I'm doing something wrong, or maybe you need to lvl up to tank properly on a pala, idk.

author: altgf
content:
ret paladin 101

- choose your spec

AP/crit - slow weapon, use Seal of Command;
stat prio - agility > strength > intellect > spell power;
get windfury, if no windfury use 2% crit stones
Hybrid - slow weapon, use Seal of Righteousness;
stat prio - spell power > agility > strength > intellect;
get windfury/flametongue
Spelladin - Manual Crowd Pummeler, use Seal of Righteousness;
spell power > agility > strength > intellect
get flametongue, if no flametongue use Shadow Oil

- get yourself Storm Gauntlets, no matter what spec you play. AP/crit doesn't need it once geared
- combine melee dps and caster dps consumables
- get yourself Wrath of Cenarius if you play Hybrid or Spelladin
- use Dragonbreath chilli as any spec
- get yourself swing timer addon
- always play this spec

content:
This is what I use in raids and is pretty much the standard give or take a few things: https://talents.turtle-wow.org/paladin/0-5IDL0J-5FUVCC0UE

Every Pally Tank that raids seriously runs some sort of 21/30 Prot/Ret build with Holy Shield and 5/5 Vengeance; whether you take Blessing of Sanc, Heart of the Crusader, Seal of Command, etc. is up to you and your playstyle. If you want to have access to Blessing of Sanctuary for easier farming without respeccing, it's a good use of one of your waisted points in Prot.

author: RIP holyprot 31/20 you were good
content:
Actual hpal main here.
On turtle we don't really worry about running out of mana because of the tea consumables. There are two of them: tea with sugar from winterspring (repeatable quest) or herbal tea purchased from hyjal with small shards.
They both do the same thing: mana and health restore that is separate from potion cooldown. Instead it uses the healthstone/demonic rune cooldown.
By using teas and major mana potions throughout a fight you should never worry about mana

author: RIP holyprot 31/20 you were good
content: I prefer to stack +heal whenever possible, because throughput is the hpal bottleneck, not mana. +heal also lets you downrank your casts to save mana. I'm at 1200 +heal and my 35 mana rank one flash of light heals for ~630 and crits for ~945

author: Ruth
content:
Time-On-Target Templar (ToT Temp)

Concept 

Time on Target Templar is a Deep Ret/Holy Build which focuses on sustain and control in combat. The best comparison is Blood DK in Wrath of the Lich King. ToT Temp can be used with any weapon (1h or 2h), however faster swing times will yield more damage since your primary seal will be Seal of Righteousness. Additionally, using a shield in your off hand will increase your durability and give you more leeway when fighting. Two-handed weapons also perform very well with this build, but you’ll get the most out of it using a skullflame shield or a Hyperchromatic Deflector. Other shields will work too. This build's crux is the ability to hard-cast a 1.3-1.5 second holy light with a reduced chance to be interrupted. PvP Trinket is recommended as rouges stuns and polymorph will be the interrupts you will not have resistance to. 

Please note that increased resistance does not mean you will never be stopped from casting. 

Weaknesses 

The only true weakness of this build is that it can be countered by CC heavy classes such as Rouge, Warlock, or the occasional Prot Warrior Specced into improved Revenge. Arms Warriors with Mortal Strike can also be annoying but do not pose as big of a threat as the previously mentioned classes. I was able to kill several skilled T3 Arms warriors with it, the only factor that altered the win rate was whether they resisted Hammer of Justice or Repentance along with the RNG from their critical Strike Rating. Mages can also be a threat with counter-spell however the build won more encounters than it lost.

author: dusty (Make Shock Live Again)
content:
OK so first off, whether or not you take Bulwark also depends on if your AoE grinding. Do you need it?  No. But there's no reason to not take it so you can pull more and kill more reliably. Plus, as a Prot it's still good to have to help your healer if things get squirrelly. 

Secondly, the only time a group won't need BoK is of there's also a Ret and you won't know there is one until you get the group unless you are queuing with a friend. But for dungeons, Imp Blessings is arguably better. Plus there's a good chance a Ret isn't going to have it since I'm pretty sure they all take the mana reduction instead.   Might makes kills faster while BoW helps healer and casters sustain longer and drink less which at lower levels, they probably will want more than Kings. Less drinking time means faster dungeons. Kings is a miniscule benefit to crit until way later and Might benefits melee more.  If you think the group needs more health than that means either you or the healer is failing.  So you should be doing improved blessings since a Ret is most likely not going to have it and leave Kings up to a Ret if you do. 

Sanctity I already covered above. It's not worth it until you have good access to SP and any Ret with a clue isn't going to have it until post 60.

You know what's really insane for your leveling experience?  AoE grinding.

author: iso
content:
ArP is a complicated topic. it depends heavily on the target's initial armor and your comp's capability to reduce it.
say you are fighting Noth and you have dedicated members for CoR/FF/IEA, now noth has 155 armor. if you use t3 boots with 100 ArP you'd get roughly 1.7% extra physical dps (in today's AP ret terms this is about 1.3%ish overall damage increase) which is pretty good.
if you use the same setup at KT you'd get 0% increase, because he is 0 armor before your ArP.
if you are fighting Ostarius with the same setup, you'd get 0.7% increase which would be considered "meh" or "not worth"

hope this makes it a bit more clear on how to approach it

author: Iseut
content:
no comprehensive guide

>BIS
still in flux since no one has really crunched the numbers on t3.5 and other kara40 loot that isn't just a bigger stat stick. generally as you're progressing through raids you'll be using a dps variant of the tier set since most non-tier pieces have no int and therefore no mana and ret paladin is super mana thirsty. without accounting for t3.5, hybrid ret uses t2.5 whilst AP ret uses t3. also carapace handguards from ouro in AQ40 from my understanding is bis for both AP ret and hybrid ret since it allows you to hit 314 weapon skill and have your glance damage be 93% instead of 81% from having 308 weapon skill

generally imo the weapon progression atleast for AP ret would be:
your pre-raid weapon (dreadforge retaliator, boneshatter maul, halberd of the bronze defender etc.) > whatever you can replace it with from ZG, Kara10, MC or BWL that's better > untamed blade (your best friend until nax) > corrupted ashbringer/might of menethil

oh yeah and both AP and hybrid ret should have wrath of cenarius, AP uses it for trash whilst i think for hybrid it's an integral part of their setup

>rotation
for bosses
judge seal of crusader, turn on SoR/SoC depending if you're hybrid/AP ret respective, holy strike for buff, consecration, repentance, crusader strike x2, refresh holy strike and then just press buttons generally. you want to use skills as they come off cool down whilst maintaining zeal and holy might. also judge your SoR/SoC

for trash
turn on SoR/SoC, crusader strike whilst spamming consecration and judging. not worth using holy strike generally since trash dies pretty fast but if it doesn't (30 seconds or more) it's worth using holy strike for buff

>talent build
i use this for AP ret https://talents.turtle-wow.org/paladin?points=FoAABAAAAAAAAAAoQAAAAAAAAAAAFATAFKYAFIFABAA=, you can take the points and put them into benediction if you're on blessing of salvation or kings duty but because often there's only around three paladins in my guild raids. i like taking improved blessings so might would give the most AP

hybrid ret i assume will be something like this https://talents.turtle-wow.org/paladin?points=FAAoBAAAAAAAAAAoYAAAAAAAAAAAFATAFKYAFAFABAA= but don't quote me on it since i don't play hybrid

author: Fjordain
content:
If you're just tanking Vek'lor as a Pally, you should still do it in an SR set. It's not very hard to get 200+ SR unbuffed. And you spam kings and JoR for threat. It's easiest in that scenario because then you can just join the melee on Vek'nilash for the swap and SoW/JoW for mana back very quickly.

You can tank both, but then you need to be full mitigation for Vek'nilash and fully health buffed for Vek'lor because those shadowbolts are going to hurt. But when you have 8k health you can soak them alright. Mana does become an issue in this case, since you can't regen much while you also need to push threat on Vek'nilash. But if you have Teas, Night Dragons, Mana Pots, on top of JoW with WFT you shouldn't be going oom.

I've done it both ways a few times

author: Mithreon
content: Generally speaking you'll want to heal with HS if there are 3+ targets in your 10yd (may overflow to about 12-13yd) range injured, but not so much injured that they may die the next second or two. Shock usage is the same, and you spam FoL while your HS is on cooldown. Which should be 3 FoLs tops per HS. Procs in melee are not different from ranged healing, you still look at Shock reset, whether you have Holy Light cast time reduction buff or not etc. Mana return from SoW starts to be noticeable on longer fights like Solnius, but if a boss dies in like 40s you don't care about SoW. You do want to judge Seal of Light onto the boss though (once), especially if you have 2p T3.

author: Dzonathan
content:
During leveling?
1) Tank at dungeon cap ex: tank DM at lvl 24 or so.
2) Ret Aura up
3) Righteous Fury up
4) Pre-buff SoW and Holy Shield
5) Approach mob
6) Holy Strike > Judge > rebuff SoW
6a) Drop Consecrate if more than one mob, rebuff Holy Shield as needed
7) Switch to next high priority mob
8) Holy Strike > Judge > rebuff SoW

- Set up your UI / Unit Frames / click cast macros in such a way than you can easily cast BoP on healers and mages who decide to go full unga bunga
- Pick up engi or Ez-throw dynamites for ranged pull option
- Use a sub 2.0 mainhand for quick mana regen via JoW/SoW. Spellstrikes help.

author: Vindaven
content:
basically never out of very rare emergencies (i.e. tank is missing 60%+ health and I have the buff that makes it 1.5sec cast).

generally if you make the addon never use holy light ever (even out of combat) - it would be better.

if you want the addon to be perfect you would make it only ever use holy light on the tank list… and only when the tank is down to ~40% health… and only if you have the holy judgement buff making it 1.5sec cast.

reason being: flash of light spam is more healing per second than holy light spam (outside of holy judgement).

and flash of light spam is also more mana efficient.

getting holy judgement requires too many global cool downs (casting seal, then judging). 2 seconds wasted right there to remove 1 second from holy light’s cast time (a net loss).

author: Jesse Potter
content:
T1 Head, Gloves and Boots for 3-set Judgement damage and 3% Hit
Soulforge Chest, Shoulder, Bracer, Belt for 4p 95 SP proc
T2 Legs
Hand of Ragnaros (obv) but that's heavy RNG so a good alternative is Obsidian Edged Blade - has 8 skill so it has 1% hit and 42 strength which is good for scaling with Kings, Divine Might and Holy Might
Hand of Justice and Blackhands Breadth trinkets - HoJ lasts until BWL with Scrolls of Blinding Light or the 200 AP active trinket in MC, Breadth until Heart of Dreams (Emerald Sanctum) which just adds 2% haste
Rings should be Don Julios if you farmed AV Rep, if not Blackstone from Princess and QSR
Neck Ogre Might, unlikely to be replaced until Ony Pendant, and after that should last until AQ40
Cloak you can get the Wardens of Time rep cloak, but if you have WFT it isnt necessary but it has good stats nonetheless, i havent looked at MC look too heavily personally, but afaik 11 str is pretty good regardless due to the aforementioned str scaling % mods
Libram should be Fervor for JoTC boost and then you can choose a different Libram temporarily, reduced Seal cost, 5 str on Consecration or 1% crit on Holy Strike until you get the MC Libram for execute phase

Enchants you should do Agi on everything because you need Crit as close to 35% as you can get, if you manage to succeed that fully buffed with SoC, as you won't reach 51% in Phase 1, you can then do Str enchants or all stats to keep a little bit of agi on rings/neck, Crusader Enchant is your obvious go-to

author: Dzonathan
content:
**Buffs:** Ret Aura, Righteous Fury, Blessing of Wisdom (if you dont have Sanc yet)
**Opener:** Prebuff SoW and Holy Shield (at 40) > Approach Mob > Holy Strike + Judgement > Consecrate
**Trash Rotation after opener:** Rebuff SoW and auto attack away. Refresh Consecrate and Holy Shield as needed. Hit current target again with Holy Strike if it will live longer than 6s. If not then save it for next mob. After your current target dies, switch to next one > Holy Strike > Judgement > Rebuff SoW. Continue until all trash cleared.  
**Boss Rotation after opener:** Rebuff SoR and auto attack away. Refresh Consecrate and Holy Shield as needed. Holy Strike > Judgement > Rebuff SoR. Delay Judgement if its CD overlaps with Holy Strike.
**Ranged Pull:** EZ-thro dynamite or Engi Grenades. If pulling caster/ranged mobs then make sure you hide behind the corner, stick out a bit, throw grenade, run back behind corner. Mobs now run to you and you have them all nice tightly rounded next to you.

author: Mithreon
content:
@Lhian For Holy some ideas:
T1 3p is good, 5p would be interesting if it was QoL instead of spellcrit since hpals have 15%+ crit with buffs by that point anyway, 8p was heavily nerfed before and could get a complete redesign since melee healing is different nowadays. Resto shamans benefit greatly from their 8p T1 in K40 too, that opens up a whole new build for them.

T2 3p is good (pls don't nerf), 5p doesn't have a place both at that point in progression and overall as we don't have a "Holy Light" spec and don't spam cast it anymore because of Mending Light+Daybreak combo. Also, 5p can be paired with 3p T3.5 and 2p T3 so there could be some "long-range caster build" potential there, the whole set has quite a bit of haste so building a haste-centric playstyle with the bonuses won't be alien, Resto druids have their 5p T2 as a cornerstone of a powerful K40 build. 8p is worse Daybreak now and should get a look-over imo.

T2.5 is mid, 3p mana return during cast is not needed for us anymore because of Illumination and crit on gear, 5p is decent but would benefit greatly from Mending Light/Daybreak interaction at that point in progression. Also a loooot of Spirit, but I guess that caters to the PvP backline playstyle or something. Overall a mana return set for a spec that doesn't really need it anymore. Shockadin build set, maybe? Idk.

T3 2p is great (pls don't nerf), 4p is mid (and not needed, many raids have several paladins for LoH) and should really be either swapped with 8p or reworked for some interesting synergy (4p can be taken with 3p t3.5 and 3p T1/T2), 6p should get its bonuses adjusted for "multi-spec" of a given class, so that for example Warriors don't receive armor all the time and have to clear the wasted buff slot with VCB blacklists, and maybe buffed on proc chance (or proc from Mending also) or buff duration. 8p as heal on cleanse is imo too weak and niche for a bonus of a Naxxramas full set, even if it can crit and proc Daybreak.

author: Dzonathan
content:
How to melee hpal. If you see all melees run in, you run in. If you see them bail out, you bail out. If you see one who stays while others run, you also bail because he's parsing. 

1) Incidis - When the entire raid is pulled in, you run out. That's it.
2) Lucifron - Follow marks, Kill first add, kill second add, kill boss. That's it.
3) Magmadar - Stick to doggo. You'll likely get feared. Pop Fire Resist Pot before fight and pop again during fight because it's likely you'll be feared into fire patches. That's it.
4) Garr - Dont stay close to small adds when they die. You'll probably stay either on boss tank and heal him or heal from afar with FoL. That's it.
5) Shazzah - Pop arcane pot. When his counterspell CD ends dont cast anything until it's on CD again. Pay attention to BigWigs. That's it.
6) Barron Geddon - Pop Fire resist pot. When he inferno's - you run. When you have the bomb, run to the wall. You can pop bubble when inferno if you want. That's it.
7) Golemagg - Stay on boss. Everyone else handles the dogs. That's it.
8) Twin Golems - Swap targets. That's it.
9) Thane - Detonation - Run out of the rune. Combustion - Run into the rune. That's it.
10) Sulfuron Harbringer - Kill adds in order, then boss. That's it.
11) Majordomo - Literally the same thing. That's it.
12) Ragnaros - When knockback - move away then back in. Probably will spam FoL from afar because you'll be told to spread out and heal MT.  Gather with others when adds spawn. That's it.

author: Grey
content:
Knightly Longsword.
It's good because it's fast (and cheap/available), and fast is good for proccing judgement of wisdom for mana recovery. Fast is also more consistent for SoR threat because you can get damage on the enemy sooner, and are less punished by misses.
Flurry Axe is better, but nobody recommends it because it's not _that_ much better and it's very expensive by comparison.
It's good until 60 because prot's auto attacks are primarily a spell delivery system, so it's fine if the white damage falls off---It's your holy strike and SoR that matter and neither are affected by weapon damage.

author: Mithreon
content:
Hpal has short cast, long cast, instant single target, and instant multi target heal. Short is Flash of Light (1.5s) that is very mana efficient and your main spam spell, long is Holy Light (2.5s) that heals for a lot and can be hastened by 1s after you judge something (Holy Judgement talent, buff stays until expended or your death), instant single target is Holy Shock with 20s cd that you can reset every 6s too if you want (Blessed Strikes talent), instant multi target is Holy Strike with 6s cd (Crusader Strike and Holy Strike share cd, it's one or the other to press) and 10yd smart targeting heal.

Melee playstyle comes with Holy Strike spam on aoe damage and proper positioning for that since the range is low + Holy Shock resets from Crusader Strike if needed. In melee you can also cast Judgement more frequently since it has short 10yd range, so that you can have more hasted Holy Lights.

author: orodoet
content:
Here's the serious answer as a HC paladin myself, leveling as an hybrid holy prot (the "immortal" build), not saying it's the best approach but it sure is some fun. You really dont need to 1v1 mobs up to lvl60, spare you the pain.
Out there are monsters you have to fear BUT there's also a lot of mobs that are really no threat to you.

- General rules of thumb: play a bit overleveled, around 2/3 below yours. You wont see results immediately, you still need to start rolling. New areas tend to have some crazy overtuned mobs (not all) but are also the richest and amazing to play. Always play with rested xp, join a guild and buy a guild tabard asap.
- make sure your connection is stable, if you know you risk to disconnect or have huge lag spikes then have a 2nd launcher open in the back with your credentials in, this can save your life since GMs wont resurrect you for DC deaths
- Talents: put your first 7 talents in holy (5 in intellect and 2 in Spiritual Focus) because Spiritual Focus + Concentration Aura (learned at lvl22) gives 100% resistance to pushback (BUT not to interrupts). At some point later on you may decide to grab some more talents like Holy Judgement and so on, it's up to you but also remember that your tankiness and damage come from Prot talents, so go for BoSanc asap (Redoubt -> Precision -> Toughness -> BoS)
- at lvl 18 you learn Seal of Wisdom, if you can hit your enemies reliably, you'll probably never run out of mana.
- what do you need to worry about? mobs that can punch, kick, stun, pummel, knock, fear, disorient you. Casters are also a nasty bunch, try to never pull those in packs but nuke them one by one and use trees/obstacles to hide from their spells

author: Grey
content:
You will 100% be able to tank as ret. The impact talents have on tanking at 15~40 is pretty negligible.
The main consideration is that you'll do somewhat less AoE threat.
Blocking does very little for you at low levels, so redoubt and holy shield aren't much mitigation to begin with.
i.e.
In Razorfen Kraul
The mob "Razorfen earthbreaker" hits for 240~310 before armor, so an average hit is about 178 with a 2her on (35% DR), 137 with a shield on (50% DR)
With the shield that drops in there, you have 17 block value, meaning a block reduces 15% physical damage.
So Redoubt, every 2 seconds, will give you an 8% chance per mob to have a 15% chance to take 85 damage instead of 100 damage for the next 5 melee hits
Holy Shield becomes a 45% chance to take 15% less damage from the next 4 hits.

In dungeons, you're going to be taking a lot more damage than just melee, usually from around 3 mobs (if not more) so holy shield will only block 4 hits out of the 12 that you'll receive from 3 melee mobs in a 10 second window
So holy shield and redoubt _combined_ might reduce your overall damage taken by like 2~4%
Toughness, same. In mail it might reduce your overall damage taken by another 2~4%
Blessing of Sanctuary, another 2~4%
Righteous Fury 10%

So early on, you'll only miss the mana regen from shield specialization and the aoe threat from righteous fury
towards 40+ you'll definitely want to consider finding a real tank, as toughness, reckoning, righteous defense, righteous strikes, etc start adding up to a lot of effectiveness

author: Mithreon
content:
@Argronok First boss can stun in melee, Free Action Potion or Bubble for that if you are close, otherwise simple wackamole. First phase is just tap healing active dps/tanks who tank the big dudes.

Second boss is your classic 3 FoL + 1 HS rotation, ticking aoe on the raid. If you get Adrenaline, run to the left column and hide behind it. Bubble won't work against the debuff.

Third boss just stand where ranged will be, unless you want to get cleaved and parse hps on the melee group. Supression room with whelps before that will be a mana gauntlet so keep track of your mana, big lizard dudes will cast aoe on the floor and hit melee. Orcs can be stunned out of cast.

After third boss it depends on the pulls, but if raid takes goblins out of the gates, keep track of the raid health and run out of fire.
After all that circus will be fourth boss, just stand where the ranged are and keep track of debuff you get. LoSing the boss in cover and healing the raid should suffice.
Also you can Holy Shock the active tank whenever the fire breath comes out.

Fith boss is tank and spank, just heal the active tank.

Sixth boss is also tank and spank, will be aoeing the raid, don't stand in front of him.

Seventh boss (Chromaggus) - dispell all debuffs, hide behid cover when others hide. Hourglass Sand can dispell the golden debuff you get, otherwise you get stunned by it repeatedly. Will need about 3 for the pull tops.

Final boss just heal the active tank and don't stand in front of the boss. If you get feared into the boss just bubble that, 4/5 times you get breathed on and die.

author: Chronicle
content:
**Hey Holy Paladins — quick question about Judgement of Light healing credit.**

I’m building a raid log site (Turtlogs-like) and ran into a logging question.

Right now, when a paladin casts **Judgement of Light**, the *player who procs the heal* gets the healing credit — not the paladin who applied the judgement.

Example:
⁨⁨⁨```
Alice casts Judgement of Light on the boss
Bob hits the boss → JoL heals Bob
→ Bob gets healing credit
```⁩⁩⁩
I can instead credit the paladin who applied the judgement, but since only **one JoL can exist**, that might incentivize judgement sniping if multiple paladins are present.
What do you think is most fair?

* Leave it as-is
* Credit the judging paladin
* Split credit between paladins
* Something else?
Looking for Holy Paladin opinions — this is about fair contribution and attribution, not parsing.

author: Grey
content:
Any chance you could implement a function to sim just the first global, which would be holy strike, auto attack, sor, jor with a chance of windfury and holy shield
Basically to find the expected average threat output, and the range from miniumum to maximum
The numbers you show here look pretty representative of overall TPS but they're pretty far off from my experience with actual gameplay
Righteous Strikes being 12.77% of tps sounds about right, Imp SoR being 2.55% of tps sounds about right

But in actual practice they're not a ~15% tps increase they're a ~30% increase to minimum opening threat
Say you have 1,000sp
Without those talents:
SoR(1.9) ~474 threat
JoR ~2002 threat
HS ~1668 threat
Auto ~150 threat
~4294 threat opener, without crits/holyshield/windfury/thunderfury

W/ those talents
SoR ~521
JoR ~2202
HS ~2710
Auto ~150
~5583 threat opener, without crits/holyshield/windfury/thunderfury

And in a lot of cases that _is_ the difference between being a tank vs having a dead DPS on pull

22 slot bag
Choker of the Emerald Lord is BiS until k40

author: Grey
content:
Rotation-wise it's just
precast holy shield before pulling the boss
use holy strike on cooldown, never delay it
use JoR 2 seconds after HS, preferably during the global from casting another ability (usually holy shield due to the way its cooldown frequently overlaps with holy strike's)
refresh SoR next global after casting JoR
Consecration r5  during remaining globals until threat is established, then use r1 if you need to consume less mana.

If paladin misses HS, all we have is JoR

author: Grey
content:
There are so many layers of stupid in this statement that I don't even know where is best to begin so I'll just pick a spot at random
It's not "50% vs 200%" it's 50% per melee hit vs 8% per spell hit
Wearing 2 3pcs gives you 2 spell hits per melee hit
So it's
sigil: ~15.4% probability per melee hit of 400 threat, or 61 threat per melee hit
8pc: 50% probability per melee hit of 213 threat, or 106.5 threat per melee hit.

On top of that, ret t2 is trash for us. No matter which pieces you pick, you'll be dropping a lot of either spellpower or stamina
The belt, pants, and bracers are unusable for us due to zero stam
The helmet, shoulders, gloves, chest, and boots also have seriously low stamina

Further, spellpower trinkets are incredibly valuable for prot and wearing sigil means you aren't wearing toep, reed, shard of nightmare, nelth's tear, etc which are all very powerful
It's MUCH better to add 204sp (reed+toep) to all of your holy damage for 15 seconds for guaranteed threat than it is to run a potentially empty trinket slot and 3 bad armor slots for a tiny % chance of 400 threat

Even if you're already going to wear 5pc prot t2 and 3pc ret t2 because it happens to be the gear you have available to you, it's still not worth wearing over briarwood reed, the worst spellpower trinket, because it simply adds more threat by itself as a singular slot
Once you add in the loss of bulk from wearing 3 pieces of ret t2, sigil loses out over briarwood reed even harder

author: Hexadin
content:
0) Before the boss encounter, you will face trash mobs that apply a debuff to melee players. This debuff causes them to deal AoE Fire damage to everyone nearby with every attack. Paladins and priests should dispel this effect.
1) The boss himself constantly summons Warden adds. These adds deal nasty AoE Fire damage over a large radius around. We killed them during the first phase, but in the second phase, he spawns them far too frequently, it feels like he summons a new one immediately after you kill the previous one.
2) Occasionally, the boss binds two players together with chains, mostly prioritizing ranged DPS and healers. These chains deal damage and apply a silence effect. To be honest, we didn't quite figure out exactly how to break them, however, it seemed like they broke more frequently when the affected players moved closer to the boss and he used his cleave attack and we killed boss after we proposed this idea, but some people still were dying.
3) After death boss resets his HP and summons additional adds. This marks the second phase, meaning he must be killed twice. Subjectively, nothing seems to change other than the fact that there are more adds.

author: Grey
content:
Yeah if any prot paladin complains about AoE threat in the current state of consecration I will smack them for being greedy and unrealistic.
I'm seeing nearly 600 threat on the first tick ~475 on the second, and that is a ridiculously good amount for one ability that hasn't even finished yet and will be stacked on top of other sources of threat
Even if some mage gets a 1500 crit with arcane explosion, that's only 675 threat, or 445tps and the mob will be taken off the mage before he gets another spellcast off

I think it's also kept in check by the way you can't gear for both 
the spellpower required for consecrate to auto-hold threat off arcane explosion spam, especially once the mage sappers.
The bulk required to hold 4 or more naxx trash mobs without getting globaled.

It's also _just_ barely enough to grab aggro, but it still requires extra support from holy shield, ret aura, sappers, FRD, etc to cover for DPS also sappering/using cooldowns/etc

And what's good is it's still nowhere near enough to blindly hold aoe threat off single target damage. If someone wants to hold 3 mobs off 3 DPS each doing single target damage on a different target, then that tank should 100% be required to get good at tab targetting.

content:
25% fortune will take your 5% chance to proc item and multiply that chance by 1.25

for ppm it's the same thing
you convert ppm to flat % based on your base weapon speed and apply accordingly


Pysan is 1ppm at 3.5 speed =>  1/(60/3.5) => 5.833% per hit  
25% fortune will make that 7.29% per hit ~= 1.25 ppm

author: PraylorSwift
content:
check the holy talenta and make sure to get ironclad and the improvements to holy strike. also judge reduces cast time of holy light.

run in with the mele, judge wisdom on the mob, seal wisdom, spam flash of light, hit holy strike on cooldown. it's a big aoe heal on everyone thats with you in the mele. depending on tier it does at least 30% of your healing. you get one holy light that you can cast as fast as a flash of light per pack basically (per casting of judgement).
as long as you can stay in the mele and are judging and sealing wisdom you will never run out of mana.

certain mobs silence in mele, you have to learn which.

in raids, since you are now running in, you now have to actually learn certain mechanics, however unlike other classes yours comes with an ignore mechanic button (bubble). certain packs or bossses you should still stay ranged.

ironclad not only completely changes what prebis or bis would be, but now also allows you to survive in the mele.

it's honestly a lot of fun, brought completely new life to holy pala.
light be with you friend
